facts.statement: Ohmdenosaurus lived during the early Toarcian age.
facts.quote: fossil_range: early Toarcian,

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Ohmdenosaurus consists of a tibia and ankle bones found in the Posidonia Shale near Ohmden, Germany.
facts.quote: The only specimen – a tibia (shinbone) and ankle – was discovered in rocks of the Posidonia Shale near the village of Ohmden.

facts.statement: German paleontologist Rupert Wild identified the remains as a sauropod in the 1970s.
facts.quote: In the 1970s, it caught the attention of German palaeontologist Rupert Wild, who recognised it as the remains of a sauropod.

facts.statement: Rupert Wild named the genus Ohmdenosaurus and its only species, O. liasicus, in a 1978 publication.
facts.quote: Wild named Ohmdenosaurus in a 1978 publication; the only known species is Ohmdenosaurus liasicus.

facts.statement: Ohmdenosaurus was a sauropod dinosaur that lived in what is now Germany during the Early Jurassic epoch.
facts.quote: Ohmdenosaurus (Ohmden lizard) is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic epoch in what is now Germany.

facts.statement: Ohmdenosaurus was one of the earliest known sauropods, possessing quadrupedal locomotion and columnar limbs.
facts.quote: One of the earliest known sauropods, Ohmdenosaurus was quadrupedal (four-legged) and already had the columnar limbs typical for the group.

facts.statement: One study concluded that Ohmdenosaurus was a eusauropod.
facts.quote: One study concluded it was a eusauropod.

facts.statement: Ohmdenosaurus was a terrestrial animal whose fossil was transported at least 100 km from the shoreline before burial.
facts.quote: Ohmdenosaurus was a terrestrial animal, and the specimen must have been transported by predators or water currents at least 100 km from the shoreline to its site of burial.

facts.statement: Rupert Wild formally described the fossil as a new genus and species, Ohmdenosaurus liasicus, in 1978.
facts.quote: In a 1978 publication, Wild determined that the dinosaur fossil belonged to a new genus and species, which he named Ohmdenosaurus liasicus.

facts.statement: The name Ohmdenosaurus is derived from the village of Ohmden and the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name Ohmdenosaurus is derived from the village of Ohmden and from the Ancient Greek σαῦρος (sauros), meaning lizard or reptile.

facts.statement: The fossil dates to the early Toarcian, approximately 182 million years ago.
facts.quote: It is therefore early Toarcian in age (ca. 182 million years ago).

facts.statement: At the time of its description in 1978, Ohmdenosaurus was one of the earliest known sauropods and the second terrestrial saurian fossil found from the Toarcian.
facts.quote: When Ohmdenosaurus was described in 1978, it was one of the earliest sauropods known at the time and only the second fossil of a terrestrial saurian to be discovered from the Toarcian.

facts.statement: Rupert Wild estimated the total body length of Ohmdenosaurus at 3 to 4 meters.
facts.quote: Wild estimated the total body length at 3–4 m, which is relatively small for a sauropod.

facts.statement: The tibia of the Ohmdenosaurus specimen is 405 millimeters long.
facts.quote: The tibia is 405 mm long.

facts.statement: The tibia preserves muscle attachment sites, including a cnemial crest projecting about 4 cm and a crista lateralis running about 13 cm.
facts.quote: The bone preserves projections that served as attachment sites for muscles, including the cnemial crest, which projects by about 4 cm from the upper front of the bone, and the crista lateralis, which runs for about 13 cm down the upper half of the shaft but is mostly broken off.

facts.statement: The medial condyle of the tibia is significantly larger than the broken lateral condyle and sits 2 to 3 cm lower.
facts.quote: The medial condyle is much larger than the (broken) lateral condyle and located 2–3 cm lower than the latter.

facts.statement: The calcaneus is circular, measuring 43 mm in diameter and 15 mm in height.
facts.quote: The much smaller calcaneus is 43 mm in diameter and 15 mm in maximal height, and circular in shape.

facts.statement: Rupert Wild identified several small elements between 5 and 30 mm in size below the tibia's lateral condyle as cartilage.
facts.quote: Below the lateral condyle of the tibia, Wild noted several other small elements 5–30 mm in size, which he identified as cartilage given their grainy and irregular surfaces.

facts.statement: Rupert Wild argued that small elements near the Achilles tendon attachment site may represent sesamoids due to the high stress experienced in that area.
facts.quote: As these elements are located close to the attachment site of the Achilles tendon, the area of the ankle that experienced the highest stresses in life, Wild argued that they may represent sesamoids (small structures embedded within tendons).

facts.statement: It is debated whether the small elements near the ankle are sesamoids or calcified pieces of the astragalus cartilage.
facts.quote: Alternatively, they could be calcified pieces of the cartilage of the astragalus.

facts.statement: Its fossils were originally described as plesiosaur remains until a 1978 review of the holotype identified them as sauropod fossils.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles se describieron originalmente como restos de plesiosáurido, hasta que una revisión del holotipo en 1978 los identificó como fósiles de saurópodos.

facts.statement: It lived on a series of islands in what is now the Bohemia region.
facts.quote: Ohmdenosaurus vivió en una serie de islas en lo que ahora es la región de Bohemia.

facts.statement: It is the only dinosaur identified from the Posidonia Shale.
facts.quote: Es el único dinosaurio identificado a partir de la Esquisto de Posidonia.

facts.statement: The nearest landmass was probably the Black Forest Massif about 100 km to the southwest.
facts.quote: The nearest landmass was probably the Black Forest Massif about 100 km to the southwest.

facts.statement: The genus authority is Wild, 1978.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Wild, 1978

facts.statement: The species authority is Wild, 1978.
facts.quote: species_authority: Wild, 1978

facts.statement: Ohmdenosaurus was a primitive sauropod that was an obligate quadruped with a relatively short neck and a robust body.
facts.quote: Ohmdenosaurus era un saurópodo primitivo. Era un cuadrúpedo obligado, con un cuello relativamente corto y un cuerpo robusto.

facts.statement: The type specimen consists of a tibia measuring approximately 405 mm in length and an estimated femur of at least 70 cm.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo de Ohmdenosaurus consiste en una tibia y un hueso astrágalo. La tibia mide aproximadamente 405 milímetros de largo con una longitud estimada del fémur de al menos 70 centímetros.

facts.statement: The estimated total body length of 4 meters is relatively small for a sauropod.
facts.quote: Esto produce una longitud corporal total estimada de 4 metros, que es relativamente pequeña para un saurópodo.

facts.statement: A re-evaluation suggests a body length of 6.7 meters and a weight of 1.3 tonnes.
facts.quote: Una revaluación del tamaño de Ohmdenosaurus sugiere una longitud corporal de 6.7 metros y un peso de 1,3 toneladas.

facts.statement: Remains were recovered from the Posidonienschiefer in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, in 1978.
facts.quote: Los restos de este dinosaurio fueron recobrados en Posidonienschiefer, Baden-Wurttemberg, Alemania, en 1978.

facts.statement: The species was named Ohmdenosaurus liasicus by Wild in a 1978 publication.
facts.quote: Wild llamó Ohmdenosaurus liasicus en una publicación de 1978.

facts.statement: The fossil dates to the early Toarcian, approximately 182.0 to 175.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, es del temprano toarciano hace aproximadamente 182,0 a 175,6 millones de años.

facts.statement: Wear marks on the disarticulated bones suggest the animal died on land before its remains were washed into the sea and buried.
facts.quote: Los huesos, desarticulados en el fósil, muestran signos de desgaste, evidencia de que el animal murió en tierra y que solo más tarde fueron sus huesos arrastrados al mar y enterrados.

facts.statement: The non-convex shape of the astragalus suggests Ohmdenosaurus was a very basal sauropod.
facts.quote: La forma del astrágalo, que no es convexa en la parte superior como lo es en los miembros derivados de Neosauropoda, sugiere que Ohmdenosaurus era un saurópodo muy basal.

facts.statement: Recent discoveries suggest Ohmdenosaurus may be less basal than previously thought and more closely related to gravisaurs.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, con descubrimientos recientes en Lessemsauridae, Ohmdenosaurus puede ser menos basal de lo que se pensaba anteriormente y estar más estrechamente relacionado con gravisaurios.

facts.statement: Ohmdenosaurus is one of the few sauropod fossil remains found in Europe.
facts.quote: Ohmdenosaurus es uno de los pocos restos de saurópodos fósiles encontrados en Europa.

facts.statement: The bones are believed to originate from the Vindelician High or the Bohemian Massif.
facts.quote: Se cree que los huesos de Ohmdenosaurus provienen del Vindelician High o del macizo de Bohemia.

facts.statement: Terrestrial environments were populated by diverse flora including Equisetaceae, Osmundaceae, Umkomasiaceae, Bennettitales, Araucariaceae, Cupressaceae, and Podocarpaceae.
facts.quote: Los ambientes terrestres estaban poblados por una gran variedad de flora, incluidas Equisetaceae, Osmundaceae, Umkomasiaceae, Bennettitales, Araucariaceae, Cupressaceae y Podocarpaceae.

facts.statement: The region experienced humid southwesterly monsoon summers and dry northeasterly trade wind winters.
facts.quote: Los veranos del sur con condiciones monzónicas húmedas del sudoeste ocurrieron en la mayoría de las tierras emergidas, lo que resultó en inviernos con vientos alisios secos del noreste.

facts.statement: Ohmdenosaurus belongs to the parent group Sauropoda.
facts.quote: Parent group: Sauropoda

facts.statement: Ohmdenosaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: The time range for Ohmdenosaurus is the Toarcian, from 182.9 to 180.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (182.9 to 180.4 million years ago)
